title: Workplace model for the oral exposure route
summary:
Human skin has a significant influence on the adhesion and transfer of hazardous substances. Properties such as skin moisture, texture and oil film determine how well substances are transferred.
Many employees are exposed to hazardous substances in their workplace, which they unknowingly transfer to various areas of their skin and/or absorb through their skin, breathing or mouth while performing their duties. To date, there are no scientific studies or standardised measurement methods that address this transmission route and its consequences. The OMORE project aims to develop and test suitable measurement methods for recording the amount of hazardous substances and the transmission route. The focus is on the transmission route of a substance from the surface to the hand and from the hand to the mouth.
Existing methods for taking samples from these areas are to be further developed and redesigned in order to provide reliable and reproducible data for work-related risk assessment.
In order to analyse transmission routes realistically, volunteers will be used in a controlled study at Fraunhofer ITEM. A non-toxic model substance (vanillic acid) will be used to simulate the work situation (transmission). This will generate usable and practical data on the oral intake of hazardous substances – a previously little-studied but significant aspect of occupational safety. Depending on their availability, participants can attend a minimum of two and a maximum of ten sessions.

interventions.name:
Depending on their availability, participants can attend a minimum of two and a maximum of ten sessions. 
The first step is to examine the efficiency of sampling from the hand.
Next, the efficiency of sampling from the skin areas around the mouth is examined.
Next, the efficiency of sampling through the mouth will be examined.
Next, the absorption of the model substance (vanillic acid) is examined by touching a surface.
Next, the transfer of substances from the hands to the mouth will be examined.
There is targeted oral (mouth) exposure. Subsequently, a sample is provided, e.g. by spitting or rinsing with water, to check how much of the substance has been transferred.

Potential oral transmission routes (via the mouth) in the workplace are should be simulated. These simulations are repeated at least 4 times and at most 12 times. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Able and willing to give written informed consent.
2. Male and female subjects, aged 18 to 65 years.
3. Overall healthy as judged by the investigator
4. Employee of Fraunhofer ITEM
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any facial skin lesions, hand skin lesion or oral mucosa lesions or dermatological diseases affecting the face or hands that in the opinion of the investigator might influence the outcome of this study. Any other disease that in the opinion of the investigator might influence the outcome of this study
2. Any concomitant medication that in the opinion of the investigator might influence the outcome of this study
3. Known allergy to model substance and latex.
4. Facial hair that might influence the outcome of the study.
5. Risk of non-compliance with study procedures
6. Suspected inability to understand the protocol requirements, instructions and study-related restrictions, the nature, scope, and possible consequences of the study
